title: U.S. House · Texas's 23rd District
area: West and South Texas, stretching from San Antonio's outskirts along the border to El Paso County.

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Tony Gonzales trailed Brandon Herrera in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary, 41.8% to 43.3%, forcing a runoff; Gonzales withdrew before the May 26, 2026 runoff, which was canceled, and Herrera advanced. Katy Padilla Stout won the Democratic nomination in the March 3, 2026 primary. Ben Mendoza, a perennial candidate who previously ran for El Paso mayor, is on the ballot as an independent.

candidates.name: Brandon Herrera
candidates.ballotNote: Led the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 43.3% of the vote, then advanced to the general election after incumbent Tony Gonzales withdrew and the scheduled runoff was canceled.

summary.text: Brandon Herrera is the Republican nominee for this open border-area seat. He is a firearms manufacturer and YouTube personality whose channel focused on firearms content has more than 3 million subscribers.

background.text: Attended Campbell College, studying pre-law, before leaving to start a firearms manufacturing business.
As of the 2024 election, hosted a YouTube channel focused on firearms-related content with more than 3 million subscribers.

candidates.researchNotes: No Candidate Connection survey on file; his campaign website was not readable in this session beyond confirming its existence.

candidates.name: Katy Padilla Stout
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 52.1% of the vote over three other candidates.

summary.text: Katy Padilla Stout is the Democratic nominee for this open border-area seat. She is an attorney with a law degree from South Texas College of Law.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Texas at Austin and a law degree from the South Texas College of Law.

candidates.researchNotes: No Candidate Connection survey on file; no detailed policy positions were located within this session's research budget.

candidates.name: Ben Mendoza

summary.text: Ben Mendoza is an independent candidate for this seat. An El Paso-area perennial candidate, he placed eighth in the 2024 El Paso mayoral general election.

background.text: Ran for Mayor of El Paso in 2024, finishing eighth in a field of eight candidates with 4.6% of the vote.
